title: Important Documents
description: Use this list, based on FEMA's Emergency Financial First Aid Kit, to gather, protect, and back up the papers you need to prove identity, file claims, and get aid.

items.text: Photo IDs: driver's licenses, passports, and state IDs for everyone
Insurance policies and cards: home or renters, flood, auto, health, and life, with agent phone numbers
Medication lists, medical records, and vaccination records
Birth and marriage certificates and Social Security cards
Proof of address and ownership: deed, lease, mortgage papers, and car titles
Bank and credit card account numbers with customer service phone numbers
Written emergency contact list, including an out-of-area contact
Military records such as a DD-214
Recent tax returns
Wills, powers of attorney, and health care directives
Pet records and microchip numbers
Photo or video inventory of your home and belongings, with serial numbers and receipts for big items
Grab-and-go folder of copies in a sealed waterproof bag in your emergency kit
Originals that are hard to replace kept off-site, such as a safe deposit box, with copies at home
Home copies in a waterproof, fire-resistant bag or safe, off the floor - check the safe's rating for paper vs. electronics
Encrypted digital backups in two places: a cloud account with two-factor login and an encrypted USB drive
Cloud backup codes written down and stored in your safe, in case your phone is lost
Cash in small bills and some coins stored safely at home
Never email unencrypted copies of Social Security cards or account numbers
Review once a year: update the inventory and ID copies, test that backups open, and refresh cash
Make sure a trusted adult knows where everything is kept
